item.title: Seeking greenlight for SCP
item.description: No one can remember what's in this library. They certainly don't remember that it has a guardian.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch: An archive of written material that has been lost to the rest of the world. Deleted files, burned documents, things like that. Some of this information would be very dangerous if it got out. The archive and its contents are usually imperceptible, but Foundation mnestics allow it and the materials therin to be seen and remembered. However, mnestic drugs are not strong enough to perceive its guardian, who does not want intruders in its archive.

Central Narrative: Researchers initially appear to have only recently discovered the skip and are making plans to have it explored and studied further. Then someone realizes that they have documentation from prior testing and exploration that no one remembers ordering. They have apparently sent multiple D-Class and MTF agents into the skip, but none of them have come out. Also, no other documentation of the existence of said personnell exists outside of DEEPWELL archives. One agent emerges from the skip physically unharmed, but showing symptoms of psychological trauma. The agent can't remember what may have caused said trauma or why they are the only member of their task force on record. The Foundation can tell something is up and suspends testing. This is not the first time this sequence has repeated, perhaps end the article with the start of a new cycle of testing and forgetting.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I really enjoy articles you have to think about to understand. I want to not actually state that there is a monster in the archive, rather I'd like to let readers figure that out on their own in a way that both makes them feel clever and accomplished and provides fridge horror type creep factor.

Additional Notes: I'm going to need help with the structure of the article if this ends up being something that interests people. I'll also need some help making the Foundation not look incompetent while preserving the mystery aspect. This needs to be something that seems reasonable for the Foundation to have misinterpreted.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] SCP Concept Critique
item.description: Memory-altering mattress, replaces memories with dreams
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Standard containment procedures and description, with background on its discovery. Interview and test logs showing how its anomalous effects were deduced, as well as further experimentation.

Elevator Pitch: A mattress/mattresses that induces vivid dreams in those who sleep in it. Upon waking up, their memories are retroactively altered to include, and frequently overridden with the contents of their dreams (e.g. a man who dreams of fishing may believe he had been a fisherman his whole life; a person who dreams of a deceased loved one believes they are still alive).

Central Narrative: A hospital gains Foundation attention after an outbreak of manic patients. Investigation leads to the discovery of the SCP. The affected patients are taken into Foundation custody to be examined so as to further understand the nature of the SCP.

The possibility of the SCP being used to treat treatment-resistant conditions is explored, leading to extensive testing. Humorous and dramatic attempts follow due to the SCP's unreliable nature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a memory-altering SCP that relies on the user's dreams to fabricate memories.

Additional Notes: I'm open to suggestions or developments to the concept and narrative.

item.title: "The Homeless Man" - SCP Idea - GL
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch:

A humanoid figure looking like a starving man.
Any human who goes near it that laughs gets attacked, bitten/ripped, and peeled by the SCP.
He's locked in a simple windowless room.

Central Narrative:

Starts off in urban Florida 2019, where the SCP was presumed to be a homeless man living on the street.
It was there for 2 years, not doing anything until it was caught trying to peel (with teeth) a local teen's skin off.
Video footage was captured (eventually uploaded online), and the SCP quickly-crawled away with the body.

+ show block
– hide block

Foundation field agents were warned and investigated after widespread local fear of SCP-XXXX online.
MTF Search-Teams found SCP-XXXX by an urban lake.
SCP's didn't eat, breathe, talk or scream, and walked on all fours similar to a spider.
It was captured by MTF. (Audio Attached)

Foundation put coverup stories, making a fake background, court charges, and sentencing.
Foundation took a list of items where SCP was recorded: Printed photos of people of ranging ages and an old coat SCP wore made of skin parts of different animals.

Research on the photos (attached) revealed the people were that of now-dead people.
People were that of children, adults, prison inmates, and one of the leading researchers of the Foundation.
Connections between lists of people could not be found by staff, but details of who they are, are given.
Hidden letters on the photos revealed words "fam", "peel", "ric", "sorrow", "controlling", "it's gone", and "give it back".
A note was found in the coat that stated "Life is given to those with lemons, a bad one is given to those with oranges".

D-class was used to experiment on the SCP, audio recordings, and experiment chart was attached.
SCP-XXXX didn't react or attack until the third experiment, where the D-Class chuckled nervously.
More experiments occurred until Foundation found out SCP-XXXX only reacts to D-class laughing at certain distances.

SCP-XXXX was watched over after every kill, in which he was seen to make shapes with the pieces of skin.
Foundation gave SCP-XXXX crayons and paper, but it only used skin to make shapes.
Recreated drawings were made (and attached), with the most identifiable ones as an orange, a house, a frowning face, and a knife.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Creepiness is from lack of info on the lore.

Additional Notes:

item.title: Unforgettable
item.description: An article about a kid who cannot be forgotten.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Emotional/Character-Based

Page Layout: Standard SCP format and addendum. The Addendum will have a journal where the main story takes place.

Elevator Pitch: My SCP shall be about a teen-aged boy (named Darcy Clover) who finds himself unable to be forgotten. All information about him has the same effect: when a person learns about it, it remains in their conscious memory forever. The memories can be ignored, but never forgotten.

The article's story will mainly revolve around Darcy's life when his anomaly manifested, shown through a digital journal he kept prior to his acquisition by the Foundation. According to his journal, Darcy was originally a normal high-school student, if a little introverted. When his anomaly manifested, however, he began to draw away from his friends and family, out of fear that they would remember him in a bad way.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The article begins with the boy's containment procedures, detailing many specific recommendations given by his lead psychologist. It then moves on to his description, noting (along with his effects) extremely antisocial tendencies and a general fear of cameras/microphones. It finally comes to a transcript of the boy's journal, where the core of the story lies.

The journal shows how he used to be a normal kid. He had mild feelings of self-doubt and issues socializing, but they never prevented him from living a normal life. That is, until his anomaly manifested. It's not known exactly when it happened, but he noticed how people began to act off around him. This "offness" became more intense over time, until people started to reference things he did that he had trouble remembering, leading him to realise that he was unable to be forgotten. He drew away from everyone he knew, drawing the attention of the Foundation as a consequence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I personally haven't seen much relating to unforgettable anomalies, so I feel this would be somewhat new. My plan is to show how Darcy's anomaly changed his personal/social life for the worse, which I think would be interesting to read/write about.

Additional Notes: I tried to keep this as succinct as possible, so let me know if there's anything related to Darcy's anomaly or life that I forgot to explain or clarify. Please tell me if I should add anything else, too! :)

item.title: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: It's an underground hell filled with blood inspired by the Buddhist "Blood Bowl Hell"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Exploration

Elevator Pitch: An MTF explores an entrance to an underground hell filled with menstrual blood in Japan seemingly filled with souls of women tortured by oni (demons). It’s similar to the Buddhist “blood bowl sutra.” There, the MTF males start to show heightened misogyny, and begin to believe that women there are being rightfully punished. Eventually, a snakelike entity convinces the men to ritually sacrifice MTF women.

Central Narrative: Starts with local Shinto priest interview, warning of it and an entity underneath. Remains of Sarkic encampment nearby (split from Blood Lotus), but abandoned. MTF consists of a female team leader and predominantly male squad body. Historical quotes from sutra. They enter, and some MTF members recognize dead loved ones. They take a DNA sample from one for HQ to analyze. They discover distraught Sarkic woman, who attacks them, attracting the attention of oni. A group of people living there save them. The people state that they have a leader trying to pacify a slumbering female yaldabaoth-esque entity. The group experiences friction with the leader, especially when a group member breaks down after seeing dead family members, and those living in the SCP state that the women there are being punished for some unknown reason inherent to womanhood. The tension increases when one member of the group attacks the team leader and she kills him in defense.

+ show block
– hide block

People argue that her leadership caused it, and even question if women are temperamentally fit to lead. Eventually they arrive at the leader, and see that he is a snakelike being who wants to provide a human sacrifice seemingly to placate the sleeping entity. Male members sacrifice some women by tossing into blood pool, but team leader escapes. She runs into Sarkicist, who states that there is no slumbering being, the people living there were former members of her sect, and the serpent does sacrifices for his own power. They’re caught and killed. HQ discovers that DNA from “souls” match missing women, not deceased relatives, and people living in the hell close in the area during disappearance (i.e. kidnapping, MTF members were deceived). Remaining MTF males found in nearby city, despite entrance blocked off (ie multiple entrances/exits).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Real-world religion ties, cult horror, social commentary, squick

Additional Notes: IK topics risky and may come off as sexist, but I’m taking care not to cross that line. IK compulsion’s frowned-upon, but this only accentuates pre-existing traits, hopefully keeping the horror.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:** Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A teenager name "Janual Grey" discovers that he's no longer a human after an unexplained blackout while camping at Acadia National Park, and later on woke up and finds himself as a reality-altering eldritch abomination.

+ show block
– hide block

Discovering his powers has made a few changes in him. Janual possesses numerous anomalous properties that not even he knows how many he has, and nature is every 24 hours passes by. If Janual doesn't consume any food that gives him the nutrition he needs, he will get driven into a state of absolute hostility, where he would go on a never-ending frenzy to satisfy his hunger, which of course that time he would begin to use more of his anomalous properties to lure humans deep into the woods. This is why he usually lures bad peoples into his territory and consumes them; this is a nature he embodies.


Central Narrative:
+ show block
– hide block

The main point here is that:

Janual wasn't actually a human at all from the start. His father is a cosmic eldritch abomination worshiped by a cult named "Servants of "Darkness" " secretly built under a church where the cult mainly focuses on worshiping a deity named "Darkness". When the cult managed to make his father manifest into reality, he disguised himself as a handsome human. He seduced his mother into having a child when she visits the church during Christmas with Janual's grandmother. After borning out Janual, he de-manifest himself out of reality to let his son, Janual, destroy the world instead of him. However, due to embodying some human natures, Janual didn't become malevolent as his father was.

After a few years, Janual's mother had witnessed him eating their neighbors in his monstrous form at the age of 3. As she started to find answers to why her son is like this, she soon discovers the truth while surfing on the web. She knows what she must do, and that is she must find a way to seal his powers from being unleashed due to worrying that he might bring apocalyptic events and was successfully to be able to seal it. However, during the past years, she slowly forgets about it.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Janual is a friend in school with SCP-105 before being held in Foundation custody.

Additional Notes: Draft is almost finished.

item.title: Unvirtual Reality
item.description: A program that will help the SCP foundation combat and learn about other SCPs, at the cost of putting others and themselves in danger.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article. Several experimental test logs added as well.

Genre: Sci-fi, Parallel Universes

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a computer program that one day appeared and automatically installed in every computer at site-XX. If run it will display the message "SCP Breach Simulator- Site XX Edition" and then create a realistic simulation of site XX, were you will play as yourself and will have to survive a SCP breach.

Central Narrative: Any computer brought into site-XX will manifest the program inside of their files, even if the computer was completely cut out from the internet and any other method of networking. SCP-XXXX cannot be deleted but any computer that is taken outside of the site will have the program erased from its files. SCP-XXXX will work on personal computers and laptops; smartphones, tablets, servers and mainframes won't manifest the program inside of their files. On the other hand anything that classifies as a personal computer, regardless of its model, year of manufacture or Operating System will manifest and be able to run the program. Older models will create more crude simulations, with very old computers generating text based descriptions and allowing the users to chose how to act with input prompts and more modern computers generating 3D environment that can even be compatible with Virtual Reality technology.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention Grabber: The program manifested after a particularly sudden and gruesome containment breach. In that breach agent XXXX mentioned how it felt as if her actions were not her own, but chosen and forced upon her by someone else. It is believed that the simulations that the SCP generates are not simulations at all, but live feed from a parallel universe where a breach is occurring. Players from this universe take control of their versions from the universe that is being shown in the computer, and the simulation will run until the breach is contained, the SCP escapes or the "player" dies. It is believed that after running a simulation SCP-XXXX will automatically install in every computer of site-XX of that particular parallel universe, spreading itself further and further.

The foundation can choose to use the SCP to conduct breaching simulations or even spy in parallel universes and steal research or information that might help their cause, but at the cost of damaging another SCP foundation from a parallel universe and spreading the SCP more and more. The more the SCP has spread the higher the chances are for the Foundation of this universe from becoming another "simulation" and suffering a breach.

item.title: Vague Memories
item.description: A phenomena that causes a person or thing to become unnaturally vague in what they're saying.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: Documents, people, writings, anything infected with the SCP becomes very unnaturally vague, but doesn't cause any other harmful side effect.

Central Narrative: The phenomena is referred to as "Vagueing" or "The Vague".

The SCP isn't a state of matter, nor does it exist physically, rather it's a strange unknown phenomena that spreads from person to person, only when they share ideas, brainstorm together, etc. It effects a person's speaking, and causes them to speak rather vague.

Not only does it effect humans, but also effects documents and anything written by "Vagued Men". Such infected manuscripts include a lost SCP-001 article, and the "11th" commandment. It has the same exact effects, causing very slurred and vague text.

The SCP does not have any other side effects, and only causes slurring in speech, and unnatural vagueness, no nausea, no coughing, no death, nothing like that.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Basic idea yet has a lot of interesting details when it comes to "documents lost to the vague".

item.title: The White Glove's Limousine
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights : Yes

Page type : SCP Article

Genre : Drama/Mystery/Horror?

Elevator Pitch :

- An SCP that takes the form of a Mercedes-Maybach S600 Pullman Guard

- It usually appears in a handful of locations between 7 p.m. and 9 p.m, especially when the streets are crowded.

- The SCP will “target” a person out on their own, from the crowd, who will then feel obligated to seek out the car. Upon the target’s approach, a single hand wearing a white glove will emerge from the interior of the vehicle and will gesture for them to get inside.

- Once the person does so, the door will close violently. The car will then start moving again.

- It will disappear after 25 minutes of driving. A hypnotic effect distracts any human observing the car for too long after its departure. Recording the vehicle is impossible.

Narrative :

+ show block
– hide block

In 2010, the Foundation received reports of a series of mysterious disappearances around the Sydney Opera House, the Wynn and Encore complex, and the Théâtre de Paris. After long months of investigation, the dispatched agents discovered the source of the disappearances : a black limousine, presumed responsible for abducting the missing persons.

In order to determine its properties, it was deemed necessary to dispatch observation teams to all the destinations at which the anomalous limousine had been spotted. The O.T. located outside the Théâtre de Paris was the first to spot the limousine;, at 8 p.m, on the 19th of may 2010. Although the doors of the vehicle were opened upon arrival, its interior was impossible to observe due to a lack of light inside the car. A few minutes later, a Caucasian man in his 20s entered the limousine. The door then seemed to shut itself violently, and the car immediately took off. Attempts at following the object were always unsuccessful : after an average of 25 minutes of observation, any agent following the car experiences a brief moment of inattention, during which the vehicle escapes from view. Filming the vehicle also seems to be impossible : all video records in which the limousine appears seem to be heavily disturbed, and hence impossible to watch. If any person other than the target gets within arm’s reach of the vehicle, the doors will immediately clamp shut, and the car will flee the scene. To this day, this is the only known way to prevent further abductions by the object.

Attention-grabber : The mysterious limousine and disappearances.

Additional notes : None

item.title: In the blink of an eye
item.description: What you see defines what you can do, what if you could see *much more*?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article/Personnel profile

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP page

Elevator Pitch:

  • Our senses define and limit how we interact with reality, they do not, however, define and limit reality itself. (aka there is more around us than meet the eye)
  • Human eyes can perceive three colors of light: red, blue and green, other colors are perceived by combining these three with the intensity of the light. Other animals have different light perception and therefore can see different colors than humans. Particularly, praying mantis shrimps can perceive between 12 and 16 light colors.
  • What happens when a human receives an experimental implant that allows them to see as many colors as a praying mantis shrimp?

Central Narrative: A high level MTF agent becomes blind after a mission and becomes the perfect guinea pig for an experimental biological implant that combines human and animal DNA to create augmented agents. The article starts with a brief description of the agent and how she lost her eyesight and how the implant was created. It follows with some logs regarding the surgery and recovery of the agent.

+ show block
– hide block

The meat of the narrative, though, is how her new eyes allow her to experience reality in a completely different way. Through personal entries on a journal she details her discoveries, they start small (new colors, night vision) and as she grows used to the new eyes they get bigger (she can see the flow of energy on living beings, see cracks and passages on reality that allow her to "teleport", see time as it passes, etc).

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • One goal here is create a new character to be used in future works on the wiki, she would make a great spy or extraction agent for example
  • Explore the growing sense of amazement and thrill someone feels when emerged on a new reality (aka my feelings when I discovered the SCP and plunged into this weird universe)
  • Expanding concepts such as the integrity of reality, time, space and other basic elements of the SCP universe and how humans and other beings interact with them

Additional Notes: None so far. Let the critiques begin!

item.title: SCP Concept: "This Last Week"
item.description: A town stuck looping the same week over and over again.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, possibly a little Horror (I think - hard to pin down)

Page Layout: Nothing incredibly special at this stage. If this ends up being my first published article, I don't want to be too ambitious and not be able to follow through without experience first.

Elevator Pitch: Time loop, town repeating for decades. No-one in town's aware it's happening.

Central Narrative: Loop - when first documented - lasted 1 week, resetting at midnight (internal date noted, but when undecided).

Log of events in cycle, taken not long into repeats. Includes local activities. Occasional person enters - unfortunates from before containment who didn't get out in time (e.g. Sole car enters. Driver confused because brother was in car in front, implying brother left town pre-midnight, while he didn't).

Affected bubble's temporal hazard, as anyone who enters becomes trapped in repeats if they don't leave pre-reset, arrival happening every time (shown with unfortunate agent). Living things from town cannot be removed, disappearing when extracted. Non-living objects can be, however, duplicates taking their place next repeat. Objects/people introduced from outside arrive at same time in later loops.

Speculated to be unstable spacetime bubble, causing repeats and leaking details from other realities, overwriting native. No cause determined.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Subtle changes between loops - only couple tiny things in given repeat (e.g. teapot's colour or someone's breakfast). Small things eventually snowball into drastic shifts over countless cycles - e.g. street names, businesses and even identities (extreme example's bartender originally documented as male replaced by woman). Log of noted changes over time provided, starting out with small things before they're moved to unseen comprehensive file, log's remainder focusing on significant alterations.

Article end: Researcher contacts superior. Too subtle to tell before, but they're now sure loop's shrinking. Not physical space, but timeframe, and events aren't exiting the loop - they're compressing, events getting closer together and causing problems. Example: Car driving through crossroads, another driving from other road seconds after. Compressed, crossings get closer until cross at same time, and either stop or crash. Regardless, it's a major change, causing butterflies. They speculate that as bubble grows increasingly unstable, timeframe will keep shrinking, events compacting until "casual density event" occurs. It's anybody's guess what happens then. As it isn't accelerating, however - and week's only shortened by minutes in decades - it's centuries before "event". It's suggested personnel prepare in case something emerges sooner.

'Emerges' is deliberate wording. Speculation that distortion/timeline leakage caused by something pushing into our reality.

Compression's resulted in short calm immediately pre-midnight, where there's no more events. Town disappears temporarily, leaving semi-circular crater. Was emergence of this that revealed compression.

Additional Notes: Still trying to get SCP approved, so any feedback's good.

item.title: Omelette of Misfortunate Death
item.description: This is and SCP that happens to be an omelet. It causes many to die because of how delicious it looks.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): OMELETTE

Elevator Pitch:
An omelette is discovered. Delicious. Many guards and researchers at the foundation go mad over this beautiful omelette.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
An omelette is discovered on the top of a statue, in the middle of a small town, in Oregon. People begin going mad for omelettes around the area. People begin dying due to over omeletting. A threat is posed. Anyone who sees the omelette becomes crazed with trying to recreated an omelette just as beautiful. No one who tries succeeds. They become mad with failure. Their brains become scrambled. What must they do to create the perfect Omelette without dying? The foundation becomes involved after a whole town dies of starvation with in a matter of days. The town had an ample food source. How did they die with all the omelettes? The source they find is this SCP. The foundation takes the omelette into confinement. They begin tests and find several interesting facts about the omelette, such as, it does not decompose. They begin to question whether or not its sentient. Many misfortunate tests happen until researchers at the foundation finally find a good use for this SCP.

Attention Getter:
Is the Omelette sentient? It's a Omelette for peat sakes, that at least sparks my attention. Will the omelette take over the world if it escapes or will it plunge everyone around it into immediate cooking failures and death?
Additional notes:
I am currently waiting on my original SCP idea to be critiqued so I decided to add another strange idea. I am new and again no matter how harsh, I would still enjoy criticism!

item.title: A new SCP I'm working on
item.description: I realize this is a bit similar to Scp 682 and others; I'm trying to make it as original as possible
item.content:encoded:
Scp 5091 is a boy who died in 1909 but came back to life in his coffin. He suffocated from lack of air, then came back. This went on until the cemetery he was buried in was dug up and he was taken in by the foundation, who now use him as to test possible cures to different poisons/diseases.

I call him Ressurection Teddy, as a nod to the legend of Resurrection Mary. Does that count as plagiarism?

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This kid isn't any stronger than a normal child, and he can be killed just the same, but nothing will keep him down permanently, even if it takes months for him to recover.

Central Narrative: The different test the foundation tests the foundation conducted on him. After being killed and coming back to life a few times, they decide to use him as a lab rat to develop cures to poisons and diseases that are currently without cures.

+ show block
– hide block

The things they've tested on him are AIDS/HIV, different types of prions, ricin, amatoxin, tetrodotoxin, and even a few anomalous diseases and poisons.

The kid was already traumatized from being buried for so long, and these tests only made things worse.

During an interview, he asks where his parents are. The doctor tells him they're likely dead, and he has a panic attack and hasn't talked since. Testing was suspended, and the poor thing is being given counseling.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: He can't be killed permanently, at least not in any way that the foundation has discovered.

Additional Notes: The 5091 number is a placeholder, I'll give it another number when I post it to the mainsite.

item.title: SCP Idea green light
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Elevator Pitch: 4 unseen ancient lineages of nautiloids are found around the Atlantic Ocean. Each one is drastically different from the other. Not only in physiology, but also in tactics, weapons, and speed.
Though they rarely interact, every five years, one individual from each of these nautiloid lineages will travel to the center of the Bermuda Triangle. After each battle, only one individual will leave the deathmatch.

Central Narrative: Four undiscovered nautiloids species were discovered fighting in the middle of the Bermuda Triangle by an international oceanography survey. They were later discovered in different parts of the Atlantics with little overlap in population overlap.

SCP-XXXX-A are conical-shelled nautiloids resembling Orthoceras in physique. Shell length is 4 meters. The arm length is 1.5 meters each arm. Skin is red with a brown shell. During Autumn, the instances of SCP-XXXX-a will migrate to the southern Atlantic until mid-April.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-B are curved-shelled nautiloids living in the Caribbean. Shell length of the instance is 1.5 meters. A protrusion of iron from a meter up extends 20cm out from the shell. Arms of this instance are a meter long and hooked. Webbing is present between the arms 20cm from the base.

SCP-XXXX-C has a shell diameter of 1 meter. Resembling a form of a modern nautilus. Grooves are present where the walls of the air chambers are located. Skin is mostly navy blue.

SCP-XXXX-D are coiled-shelled nautiloids with a shell diameter of 2 meters. The shell is a gradient of orange and yellow with a black rock outer layer on it. Arms of SCP-XXXX-D instance are retracted and have microscopic hairs. Arms extend to 5 meters when in use.

Every 10 years, a ritual of fertility will be held by each instance of SCP-XXXX at the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The ritual ends until the last instance is alive. The sole survivor of the ritual, for example, an instance of SCP-XXXX-B, will have a population boom of three years for its instance.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Humans know more of what’s above them than what’s below the deep oceans. The oceans are scary indeed. About 90-97% of the ocean is still undiscovered. The ocean is the last frontier to travel on this planet. Many creatures are left undiscovered to this day.

Additional Notes: Draft is almost complete. Sketches of the entities will come soon.
